report.summary: Both failures come from one product bug: book listing is not scoped to the owner. With the leak_books seeded bug active, GET /api/books and the UI bookshelf return every user's books, so the API test sees another user's book and the new UI user sees a row they never created. Fix app/main.py list_books first, and confirm whether the CI environment is setting BUGS=leak_books, since the workflow does not set it.

causes.title: Book listing returns every user's books (leak_books path)
causes.explanation: list_books() has a branch that selects all rows from the books table with no owner filter when the 'leak_books' flag is in BUGS. Both the JSON API (/api/books) and the server-rendered /books page call list_books(), so a user sees other users' books. In the API test, user 2's book appears in the other user's list. In the UI test, a brand-new user (who has created no books) sees a book row titled 'From API-7c13d5e3' owned by someone else, so the empty-state element is never rendered. The owner-filtered query in the else branch is correct, so the defect is the flag-driven leak, not the test. This is deterministic, not timing-related. The failing assertions are the isolation checks the tests exist to make.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:42: assert book["id"] not in other_ids  ->  E   assert 2 not in [1, 2]
app/main.py:163-164: if "leak_books" in BUGS: rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()
app/main.py:166: else branch filters with WHERE owner_id = ? (correct behaviour, bypassed when leak_books is set)
app/main.py:11: leak_books       GET /api/books returns every user's books
tests/ui/test_login_ui.py:14: expect(books.empty_state).to_be_visible()  ->  Error: element(s) not found
Aria snapshot in the UI failure lists a table row: row "From API-7c13d5e3 Robot Delete" for a freshly registered user

app/templates/books.html:29-30: the empty-state

only renders when the books list is empty, so the leaked row explains its absence
app/main.py:270: render_books passes list_books(user["id"]) to the template, so the UI uses the same leaking path
causes.suggested_fix: Ensure the leak_books flag is not enabled in the CI test environment (check the runner env and any BUGS setting). Then remove the leak_books branch from list_books() so the owner-filtered query is always used. Add a regression check that a second user's list excludes the first user's books. Rerun both suites to confirm.
